package main

// CHAOS-5156: lizard's condition_counter is purely token-based, not
// construct-aware -- a bare "while" token counts as a condition even used
// as an ordinary identifier (Go has no while keyword at all, only for).
// This fixture exists so goConditions["while"] has SOMETHING exercising
// it IN A GO-ONLY FIXTURE -- codex round r2 on #2266 found that the
// unfiltered coverage-manifest scan let a Rust fixture's real `while`
// silently satisfy Go's own "while" entry too, which the new
// assertEveryConditionExercisedByFilteredCorpus (clike_parity_test.go)
// no longer allows. Measured directly against real lizard 1.23.0:
// complexity 3 (base 1 + if + while-as-bare-identifier).
func while() int {
	if true {
		return 1
	}
	return 0
}
